text:
alex: Heads up — us-west-2 gpu capacity is saturated, autoscaler reports repeated scale failures. Seeing a huge steady queue for inference and a bunch of pods Pending in `research` namespace. Anyone oncall?

priya: I'm on it. Can you paste the `kubectl get pods` for the pending ones?

alex: pasted: ```
NAMESPACE   NAME                                   READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
research    hparam-search-2026-03-18-0            0/1     Pending   0          12m
research    hparam-search-2026-03-18-1            0/1     Pending   0          11m
inference   model-serving-abc                      0/2     Pending   0          3m
```

marco: autoscaler logs show repeated API throttles creating nodegroup: `ThrottlingException: Rate exceeded` from cloud provider between 09:02-09:08. It queued scale ops but never provisioned.

opsbot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-18-uw2-gpu-surge (sev=2) — link https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-03-18-uw2-gpu-surge

dani: Noted the `hparam-search` jobs use `priorityClass: system-node-critical` (ugh) and request 8 GPUs per pod. That explains lockout. They also have `podDisruptionBudget` preventing eviction.

kyle: Running quick emergency mitigations: 1) remove high priority from those jobs 2) patch pdb to allow eviction 3) taint nodes used by research to avoid new allocations. Will run with `kubectl patch` now.

priya: Commands I ran: ```bash
kubectl -n research patch priorityclass hpc-priority -p '{"value":0}' || true
kubectl -n research delete pod hparam-search-2026-03-18-0 --grace-period=30
kubectl -n research patch pdb hparam-pdb -p '{"spec":{"minAvailable":0}}'
```

alex: After evicting two jobs, pending inference pods started scheduling but still slow. Autoscaler still showing failed launches due to ENI quota hit for that region. Cloud console shows ENI limit at 60/60.

marco: Spun up emergency nodepool `uw2-gpu-emergency` with different instance family (p4 -> g5) to avoid provisioning contention and with prefix elastic-network-interface overrides. Cloud API accepted that launch.

dani: FYI that means slightly higher cost but avoids waiting on quota. I've alerted finance lead.

kyle: After new pool created, we saw 6 new nodes join and the pending queue drained. Model-serving pods are now Running.

mia: Notes for postmortem: 1) research jobs shouldn't use system-level priorityclass 2) add quota checks to CI for ENI capacity before fleet-wide scale 3) autoscaler should surface throttling as a metric/alert 4) consider CNI mode with ENI overprovision guard

priya: Adding short-term policy: block creation of pods requesting >4 GPUs in non-scheduled namespaces; will submit policy MR in infra repo.

alex: Thanks everyone. Summary: runaway hparam job + ENI quota + cloud throttling blocked autoscaler => evictions + emergency nodepool (different instance family) fixed service. Follow-ups: ops postmortem and quota alerting. :thumbsup:
